newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LEU INCHES DOWN, CEN.BANK MOPS UP FUNDS.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LEU INCHES DOWN, CEN.BANK MOPS UP FUNDS.

text.p: 1340 GMT - The Romanian leu closed just down at about 7,155/200 to the dollar on Monday against 7,140/180 in the morning amid slack interbank trading, operators said.
They said the slide of the leu-dollar rates followed dollar purchases by the central bank (BNR) which continued to drain excess dollars from the market.
Traders said the BNR's bid for its dollar purchases was at 7,160 lei to the dollar, compared to 7,155 last Friday.
The money market remained unmoved by the BNR move to cut its key rates -- the discount rate to an annual 40 percent from 50 percent and the Lombard rate to 140 percent from a previous 200 percent.
Short-term money market rates remained fairly stable near 30 percent against some 60 percent a few weeks ago due to a leu overliquidity.
Traders said the BNR had soaked leu funds taking leu deposits from banks at rates hovering near 32 percent in a bid to prevent a further falls in short-term money market prices.
Leu-dollar retail rates were slightly down at about 7,100/150, from morning levels of 7,050/150. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
